evidence: app/src/pages/abilities/[name].astro — entire feature is one route file; deleting app/src/pages/abilities/ removes it
app/src/layouts/Base.astro:21-25 — nav is centralized; there is no Abilities link to unlink
app/src/pages/pokemon/[name].astro:107-116 — the only other touch: the Pokémon page's Abilities section links to /abilities/*
app/src/lib/pokedex.ts:96-101 — cardsForPokemon's note callback was built for abilities but is generic; no ability-specific lib code to delete

evidence: app/src/components/CardList.astro:14 — single render point for sprites/dex numbers, so one fix covers home, moves, abilities, types and team card lists
app/src/lib/pokedex.ts:106-107 — but Card.id doubles as pokemon id and species id; splitting sprite-id from dex-id means touching the Card type, both builders and CardList

app/src/components/TeamButton.astro:16-25 and app/src/pages/team.astro:44-53 — readTeam/writeTeam cookie logic duplicated in two inline scripts with 'team' and size 6 hardcoded, plus app/src/lib/team.ts:3 — three places define team semantics
app/src/pages/moves/[name].astro:31-33 vs app/src/pages/abilities/[name].astro:22-24 — effect-fallback chain and DASH/show helpers duplicated per page
changeability.rationale: Render-level fixes have one obvious home (CardList), but the team cookie contract and the effect/404 page pattern are duplicated, so those fixes land in 2-3 synchronized places.

evidence: app/src/lib/pokedex.ts — one 140-line module mixes pure formatters (humanize, dexNumber), list fetchers and card builders; every page and team.ts import from it

app/src/pages/index.astro:102-109 — client scripts depend on server markup via magic IDs (#results, #moves-content in MovesSection.astro:196-197, #team-content in team.astro:94-95) and data-* attributes
app/src/lib/team.ts:9-20 — team state is explicit server-side (cookie parsed in one place per page), but client scripts re-parse document.cookie independently
app/src/components/CardList.astro:1-10 — components take narrow Props and depend only on lib helpers; no component reaches into another's internals
coupling.rationale: Server/client separation is otherwise clean (all fetching in frontmatter/lib, scripts only touch DOM), but the wide pokedex.ts module, the implicit element-ID contract, and the triplicated team-cookie state keep this at some tangles.

evidence: app/src/lib/pokedex.ts:96-113 — cardsForPokemon unifies pokemon-refs from types/moves/abilities into species cards with a note callback: designed around the app's real variation
app/src/components/CardList.astro:6-10 — one card component serves five lists via optional types/note/removable; no flag-parameter creep beyond one boolean
app/src/components/MovesSection.astro:1-118 — ~200-line monolith mixing version-group fetches, table shaping and markup; an Items section shaped like Moves would be copied, not reused
app/src/pages/moves/[name].astro:16-35 vs app/src/pages/abilities/[name].astro:15-24 — detail pages hand-roll the same fetch→404→h1→facts-dl→effect pattern with no shared resource-page seam
abstraction_design.rationale: The Card/CardList and cardsForPokemon abstraction is genuinely good; the detail pages and MovesSection are copy-paste-shaped rather than parameterized, which caps how far the existing abstractions stretch.

findings.issue: Team cookie semantics (name 'team', max size 6, dedupe) are re-implemented in two inline client scripts and once server-side in app/src/lib/team.ts:3-20; the client copies hardcode what the server module exports as constants
findings.suggestion: Extract a small shared client module (e.g. src/lib/team-client.ts) that TeamButton.astro and team.astro both import, keeping TEAM_COOKIE/TEAM_SIZE in one place

findings.issue: The fetch → DOMParser → swap-fragment progressive-enhancement pattern is duplicated across three inline scripts (also app/src/components/MovesSection.astro:191-202 and app/src/pages/team.astro:89-100) with per-page element IDs forming implicit contracts
findings.suggestion: Factor one client helper like swapFragment(url, selector) into a shared script module and reuse it in all three spots

findings.issue: MovesSection mixes version-group fetching, table shaping, markup and client sorting in one ~200-line component; a similar-but-different section (e.g. Items tables) can only be created by copying it
findings.suggestion: Split row shaping (pure data) from markup, and parameterize the sortable-table renderer so future tables reuse it

findings.issue: Detail-page pattern (api fetch → null/404 → NotFound → Base → h1 → facts → effect fallback) and the show()/DASH helpers are duplicated across move, ability and type pages
findings.suggestion: Introduce a thin DetailPage component or shared helpers (facts dl, effect fallback, show) so resource pages stop repeating the same scaffolding

findings.issue: pokedex.ts mixes pure formatting helpers (humanize, dexNumber, DASH) with list-wide data fetchers (getHomeEntries, getGenerations), giving a wide import surface and making the module a hub everything depends on
findings.suggestion: Split into a format.ts (pure) and a data.ts (fetchers); pages then depend on narrow modules

findings.issue: Card.id is used both as the sprite Pokémon id and the species id for the dex number, which is only equivalent because default Pokémon share the species ID; a data change or form-awareness fix must touch the Card type, both card builders and CardList
findings.suggestion: Name the field explicitly (e.g. pokemonId vs speciesId) now, while there's one builder and one consumer, so the two concerns can diverge cheaply

summary: A clean, idiomatic Astro 7 SSR app with a genuinely well-designed card pipeline: every Pokémon-card list funnels through one component and one data helper, so most card-level changes land in a single place. The weaknesses are duplication rather than entanglement — team-cookie logic in three places, the DOM-swap enhancement pattern in three scripts, and per-page copy-paste of the detail-page scaffolding. A shared client module and a thin resource-page seam would move this from comfortable to exemplary.
